Definition: from G473 and G4008; on the opposite side:--over against.
BiblicalUsage: Paul's ship sails over against Chios on its way to Jerusalem, holding its course on the far side of the island. The word means on the opposite side, across the water from where you stand.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for the opposite shore carries no doctrine of its own; its interest is the voyage, that the ship made for the country on the far side.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
